title: Washing cars, bellboy work and tips as a young entertainer
summary: At fourteen he also washed cars and was a bellboy, earning tips and a local name as an entertainer with his ukulele.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But wait a minute. Further, to make money, to show you how my life was always -- I was always trying to do something for myself, you know, to be independent. I also became very good at washing and polishing cars, which I got an extra fee for this, naturally. And I'd take the cars in the back and wash them up and shine them up, and some of the very nice guys would let me take the car for dinner and I'd go and show off in front of the girls in school. You know, they'd think I had a new car every day. You know, this made me a little popular with the girls, too, you know.
Of course.
So I was beginning to like girls, you know.
Sure.
As every boy does, you know.
That's right.

He can't get rid of that feeling, you know, so easily, you know. Right? So all this was a part of my having fun, and actually as I said this is before I had noticed this vicious thing. I was happy and enjoying myself, and my music was what did it because my music put me in such a realm above everything that I didn't even hardly see these ugly things.
No.
Because I was so busy having fun, and it didn't strike me individually, see.
That's right.

So I was having fun as a young boy. So in the process all of the entertainers that came there, I was also bellboy. Now, how do you like that, at 14 years old? I was a shoe shine boy, I was the porter, and I helped bells at night. Right?
Right.
All of which I got about $2.50 a day, maybe a week. I don't know. But I got tips, you know, and I played my little ukelele. So all the entertainers, they knew
me, and you know, I got these little tips, and you know, made a little name for myself in the town there.
Yes.

As an entertainer. And I'd play my ukulele, sing one of my songs, you know. (Singing). You know, what I mean, pop my little rag. Right? So that's really how I got introduced to the entertainment business period, I mean, you know, gradually I was getting into it then, before I told you I went to Columbia, Missouri, to high school.
Right.
See, I was in grade school during this time.
Yes.
But don't you think that's very interesting?
Yes, I do.
I don't know how I forgot that.
So I mean you had a real first taste of the entertainment world, didn't you? Yes.
That's right.
